guards_arrive.note: Guards of Varenholt come looking for the girl. The hero refuses to give her up; the fight is ordinary combat, begun on the last beat.

beats.text: The barking stops all at once. In the silence there are boots, a great many of them, and the creak of leather.
A fist hammers on the door of the inn. The innkeeper looks at you, and does not move.
The door is thrown open. Red cloaks fill the doorway: a sergeant, and two guards of Varenholt with their hands on their swords.
[[YELLOW]]Sergeant Havel speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Captain. Or whatever you are now. Varenholt has been looking for you."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Sergeant Havel speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"The king wants the girl. The summoner's brat. Give her up, and you can walk out of here. Nobody needs to say you ran."[[/]]
You stand. Your hand finds the hilt of the dark blade, and stays there. [[BLUE]]"She is a child. She stays with me."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Sergeant Havel speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Then it is desertion, and treason, and I am sorry for it, Captain. I mean that. Take him alive, if you can."[[/]]
[[RED]]Three blades come out of three scabbards at once.[[/]]

after_the_guards.note: The guards are beaten: the innkeeper, Ryn waking and choosing to come along, and a word about a woman asking for the hero.

beats.text: The last guard goes down, and the inn is quiet but for your breathing and the shutters rattling in the wind.
The innkeeper comes out from behind the counter, grey in the face, a heavy pan still in one hand. She looks at the floor, and then at you.
[[YELLOW]]The innkeeper speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Twenty years I have kept this room, and nobody has ever drawn steel in it. Go on. See to the girl. I will see to the floor."[[/]]
A small sound from the back room. Ryn is sitting up on the pallet, her face the colour of ash, staring through the curtain at what is on the floor.
[[YELLOW]]Ryn speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"You stood in front of them. I heard all of it, through the wall."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Ryn speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"They were going to take me back to him. Weren't they."[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"Not while I am standing."[[/]] You wipe the blade, and mean it.
[[YELLOW]]Ryn speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Mother is gone. The village is gone. I have nowhere left to go."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Ryn speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"If you will have me, I would rather go where you go. And I can help. Mother taught me more than the calling."[[/]]

[[YELLOW]]The innkeeper speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"If you are the dark-bladed captain from the king's city, there is something you should know. A woman came in off the Saltreach road three nights ago, half out of her mind with fever. She keeps asking for a man with a black sword. Old Orrin and Maren took her in. Their house has blue shutters."[[/]]

sickroom_visit.note: The first time the hero goes into the back room of Orrin and Maren's house: Rosalind, sick with salt fever, and what it will take to cure her.

beats.text: The back room is dim, and smells of vinegar and crushed herbs. An old man stands beside a narrow bed, and does not look round as you come in.
Someone is lying in it. Even in the half-dark, grey and shining with fever, you know the line of her face.
Rosalind.
[[YELLOW]]Rosalind speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Is that... you? You came. No... I came. I came to find you."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Rosalind speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"They said the ships had gone south. I took the road. And then the whole mountain came down."[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"Rest. I am here."[[/]] Her hand finds yours, hot as a stone left in the sun, and holds on.
[[YELLOW]]Orrin speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"We found her at the edge of the wash three nights back, half buried, talking about a man with a black sword. Maren has not left her side since."[[/]]

[[YELLOW]]Orrin speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"It is the salt fever. It comes up out of the wash in the hot months and it does not let go. She will not see the month out. Not unless you can fetch a mirage pearl."[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"Where?"[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Orrin speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Ask me. There is more to tell, and she should sleep."[[/]] (talk orrin)

rosalind_cured.note: The mirage pearl is given to Orrin; the fever breaks.

beats.text: Orrin crushes the pearl into the cup, and Maren holds it to Rosalind's lips. Nobody breathes.
For a long time nothing happens. Then, slowly, the shine goes out of her face, the way frost goes off a field.
[[YELLOW]]Rosalind speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"...You look terrible."[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"You look better."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Rosalind speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Stay out of trouble until I can stand. That is an order."[[/]]

meet_belaric.note: At the foot of the sinkhole the hero meets Belaric, a sage of Ashmere trying to get through the Brineway; he joins the party.

beats.text: The sinkhole's throat opens into a cave full of the sound of dripping, and of someone swearing quietly in two languages.
An old man in a soaked grey robe crouches over a map spread on a rock, a black staff across his knees and a lantern at his feet. He looks up, and does not seem at all surprised.
[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Another one. They told me nobody came down here any more. Are you lost, or only stupid?"[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"I am looking for a mirage pearl."[[/]]

[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Ha! A better reason than mine, and a worse one. The royal house of Ashmere guards the secret of the pearls, or it did when I sat at its table: where they come from, and how one is got. If anyone can tell you, it is the royal house, and that is where I am going. I am Belaric. I was a sage at its court, before I was an old man in a hole."[[/]]

[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"I am going through to Ashmere. There is something at the far end of the Brineway that does not want company, and I cannot go round it a third time. I have the spells. I have not the knees. You have the knees."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Walk with me through the Brineway, and I will see you to your pearl. Fair?"[[/]]
[[BLUE]]"Fair."[[/]] He folds the map with a snap, and the staff comes up like something that has been waiting.
[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Then do not stand about. The water rises on the hour, and I have no wish to be rescued by someone who is still working out where the exit is."[[/]]

camp_in_the_dry_hall.note: The midpoint: a vast empty dry hall where the party makes camp for the night; ends on a prompt to talk to Belaric.

beats.text: The tunnel opens, and keeps opening. You stop at the threshold of a room so large the lantern does not find the far wall.
The floor is dry. After half a day of wet stone, dry sand underfoot is a shock. Pale columns stand in rows, some fallen, and the air does not move at all.
[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"The Dry Hall. It has never flooded, and nobody knows why. It is the only place down here where you may sleep without waking up wet."[[/]]
[[CYAN]]You make camp against the largest of the fallen columns. Ryn finds dry reeds, Belaric strikes a flame from the head of his staff, and the dark draws back to the edge of the light.[[/]]
The old man sits with his back against a column and his eyes on the fire, and for a long time he does not speak. (talk belaric)

camp_morning.note: After the camp conversation: the night passes, and Belaric teaches Ryn lightning.

beats.text: [[CYAN]]The night passes.[[/]]
You wake to a grey light from nowhere: the pale fungus on the columns glows at dawn, as if the hall had a sky after all.
[[YELLOW]]Ryn speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Belaric... would you show me again? The white fire. I was watching your hands all night."[[/]]

[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Hm. Hold the staff... no. Like this. Do not think about it; think about the sky going white. Mother taught you the calling, did she not? It is the same listening, only upward."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"On your feet. I have talked enough for a month. The water will be rising again, and I would like to have drowned something before breakfast."[[/]]

warn_brine.note: The warning at the Brine Gate; the next try east goes through, into the Drowned Gallery.

beats.text: [[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"That is the door. Beyond it is the Brinecoil. I have been standing in front of this arch twice in my life, and twice I have turned round."[[/]]

[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"It comes up out of the water, and goes down again, and while it is down nothing you do will touch it, and it answers any who try. Strike when it rises. Wait when it sinks. Do you understand?"[[/]]
[[RED]]There is no turning back once the gallery closes behind you. If there is anything left to do, do it now.[[/]]

brinecoil_rises.note: The Drowned Gallery closes behind the party and the Brinecoil rises: eight legs first, each attacking on its own, then the head.

beats.text: The causeway is narrow, and the black water on either side does not move. Ahead, the steps up the far wall are plain to see, and a long way off.
Behind you, with a groan of old stone, the arch swings shut.
The water on both sides of the causeway begins to bulge.
[[RED]]Something vast and grey-green hauls itself up out of the lake, and eight great limbs thrash up out of the water around it.[[/]]
[[RED]]And the head comes up between them, and opens a mouth like the mouth of a well.[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"The legs first! They are soft, and they are afraid of nothing but lightning. Burn them, and then the head will be a smaller problem!"[[/]]

brinecoil_falls.note: The Brinecoil is dead: the way east opens, and Belaric says what is beyond it.

beats.text: The Brinecoil's head sags, and the whole vast body slides back into the lake and does not rise again. The water goes still, and then, slowly, clear.
At the far end of the gallery, where the steps climb out of the dark, a thin grey light has begun to move on the water.
The arch behind you grinds open.

[[YELLOW]]Belaric speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Thirty years. Thirty years I have been afraid of that, and it died in a quarter of an hour. Ha. Ha! ...Come. Ashmere is on the other side of those steps. And my daughter."[[/]]
